children: are rising as the company's shares reach new highs, says Jefferies, despite growing enthusiasm over its potential to benefit from wider adoption of voice-based AI.
TWLO is down 2% in Wednesday trading. Shares have gained 95% so far this year.

The brokerage said the key questions ahead of Twilio's third-quarter results are whether gross profit growth can accelerate, whether personal AI assistants will drive demand for voice AI infrastructure, and whether large cloud providers could pose a greater competitive threat. Twilio is expected to post earnings on 30th October.

Jefferies expects gross profit growth of 19% in the third quarter and said growth of 20% or more is possible, helped by a stronger business environment and the continued rollout of higher-margin voice AI revenue.

The brokerage also said the growing use of AI assistants that can make phone calls could support Twilio's business over time. It said Twilio could benefit from wider adoption of voice AI regardless of which specific AI platforms use its infrastructure.

Jefferies said investors have also renewed concerns about competition from major cloud providers after Microsoft introduced a product that competes with ElevenLabs, a company active in voice AI technology.
The brokerage said it does not see a near-term threat to Twilio, arguing that the company's role in voice AI extends beyond the services provided by ElevenLabs.

title: Twilio rally fuels investor concerns ahead of earnings, Jefferies says
